chapters.title: Foreign Trade Policy 2023: Basics and Export Promotion Schemes
chapters.summary: Legal framework of foreign trade, features of FTP 2023, status holders, Advance Authorisation, DFIA, EPCG, RoDTEP, EOUs and deemed exports, with export obligation and value addition computations.
chapters.lawAsOf: Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act 1992 and Foreign Trade Policy 2023, as updated to 2026

lesson.heading: Legal framework and features of FTP 2023
lesson.body:
The **Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992** empowers the Central Government to make the Foreign Trade Policy (section 5) and to regulate imports and exports. The **Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)** administers it. No person can import or export without an **Importer-Exporter Code (IEC)** (section 7), which is a 10-character code based on the PAN.

**FTP 2023** came into force on **1 April 2023**. Unlike earlier policies, it has **no end date**; it is updated as needed. Its approach rests on four pillars:

- **Incentive to remission:** schemes that refund embedded taxes (RoDTEP, RoSCTL) instead of giving rewards.
- **Export promotion through collaboration:** exporters, States, districts and Indian missions; **Districts as Export Hubs** and **Towns of Export Excellence**.
- **Ease of doing business:** online, automatic approvals, lower fees and fewer documents.
- **Emerging areas:** e-commerce exports (higher value limit for courier exports), merchanting trade, and dual-use items (SCOMET).

**Status holders** are recognised exporters with privileges such as self-certification and priority clearance. Under FTP 2023 the export performance thresholds (in USD million, over the current and previous three years) are: One Star 3, Two Star 15, Three Star 50, Four Star 200, Five Star 800.

lesson.heading: Duty exemption schemes: Advance Authorisation and DFIA
lesson.body:
**Advance Authorisation (AA), chapter 4:** allows **duty-free import of inputs physically incorporated** in the export product (plus fuel, oil and catalysts consumed in the process), with an allowance for normal wastage. Inputs are fixed by the **Standard Input Output Norms (SION)** or on the basis of a self-declaration (ad hoc norms).

| Feature | Advance Authorisation |
| --- | --- |
| Duties exempted | BCD, additional duties, SWS, AIDC, IGST, compensation cess, and anti-dumping, safeguard and countervailing duties where applicable |
| Minimum value addition | **15%** (higher for some items) |
| Validity for import | 12 months from issue |
| Export obligation period | 18 months from issue |
| Condition | Actual user; inputs cannot be transferred, even after export obligation is fulfilled |

**Value addition (para 4.08):**

VA = (A - B) / B x 100, where A = FOB value of the export realised and B = CIF value of inputs covered by the authorisation plus value of any other imported inputs used.

**Duty Free Import Authorisation (DFIA):** similar to AA but exempts **only BCD** (IGST and cess are paid and taken as ITC); minimum value addition 20%; the authorisation or the imported inputs become **transferable** after export obligation is fulfilled.

**Worked example.** Inputs CIF ₹1,00,00,000 imported under AA; export FOB realised ₹1,25,00,000. VA = (1.25 crore - 1 crore) / 1 crore = 25%, which meets the 15% minimum.

lesson.heading: EPCG, RoDTEP, EOUs and deemed exports
lesson.body:
**Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG), chapter 5:** import of capital goods (including spares, tools and software) for pre-production, production and post-production at **zero customs duty**, subject to:

- **Specific export obligation:** **6 times** the duties, taxes and cess saved, to be fulfilled within **6 years** from the date of issue of the authorisation.
- **Average export obligation:** the authorisation holder must also maintain his average export level of the preceding 3 years for similar products.
- **Domestic sourcing:** if capital goods are bought from Indian manufacturers, the specific export obligation is **25% lower** (75% of normal).
- Exports must be of goods made with the capital goods (or services rendered with them); the actual user condition applies until the obligation is met.

**RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products):** refunds central, State and local duties and taxes **embedded** in exported goods that are not refunded under any other scheme, such as VAT on fuel used in transport, electricity duty, mandi tax and stamp duty on export documents. Rates are notified as a percentage of FOB value (with per-unit caps for some items). The benefit is credited as a **transferable electronic duty credit scrip** in the exporter's ICEGATE ledger, usable to pay BCD on imports. **RoSCTL** does the same for apparel and made-ups.

**EOU, EHTP, STP and BTP (chapter 6):** units that export their entire production (with permitted domestic sales) and must be **net foreign exchange positive** over 5 years. They can import and procure inputs and capital goods duty-free.

**Deemed exports (chapter 7):** supplies where goods do not leave India but payment is received in rupees or foreign exchange, such as supplies to AA holders, EOUs, EPCG holders and specified projects. Under GST, notified deemed export supplies (section 147 CGST) are taxed, and the supplier or recipient can claim refund.

**Common mistakes:** computing EPCG export obligation on BCD only (it is on all duties, taxes and cess saved, including IGST); applying the AA value addition formula to FOB of imports; treating DFIA as exempting IGST; and treating AA inputs as transferable.

keyPoints: FT(D&R) Act 1992: section 5 FTP, section 7 IEC (10-character, PAN based). FTP 2023 from 1 April 2023, no end date.
AA: duty-free inputs physically incorporated; exempts BCD, SWS, IGST, cess and trade remedy duties; VA at least 15%; import validity 12 months, EO 18 months; actual user.
VA = (A - B) / B x 100, A = FOB realised, B = CIF of imported inputs.
DFIA exempts only BCD; VA 20%; transferable after export obligation.
EPCG: zero duty on capital goods; EO 6 times duties, taxes and cess saved in 6 years; 25% less for domestic sourcing; plus average EO.
RoDTEP: remission of embedded taxes not otherwise refunded; % of FOB; transferable e-scrip used for BCD.

cases.title: Case: Sunrise Auto Exports Pvt Ltd
cases.body:
Sunrise Auto Exports Pvt Ltd, Chennai, makes auto components for export. In 2026-27:

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Capital goods imported under an EPCG authorisation; duties, taxes and cess saved (BCD, SWS and IGST) | ₹80,00,000 |
| Inputs imported duty-free under Advance Authorisation, CIF value | ₹2,00,00,000 |
| Export of components made from those inputs, FOB value realised | ₹2,60,00,000 |

Sunrise has also exported other goods eligible for RoDTEP.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is correct?
options: It is valid for five years, from 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2028
It came into force on 1 April 2023 and has no end date
It is made by CBIC under the Customs Act
It replaced the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992
questions.explanation: FTP 2023 took effect on 1 April 2023 and, unlike earlier five-year policies, is open-ended and updated as needed. It is notified by the Central Government under section 5 of the FT(D&R) Act 1992 and administered by DGFT.

questions.prompt: How does the Duty Free Import Authorisation (DFIA) differ from the Advance Authorisation?
options: DFIA exempts only basic customs duty and becomes transferable after the export obligation is met
DFIA exempts IGST but not basic customs duty
DFIA has no export obligation
DFIA is available only to status holders
questions.explanation: DFIA exempts only BCD (IGST and cess are paid and taken as ITC), needs 20% value addition, and the authorisation or inputs become transferable once the export obligation is fulfilled. AA exempts BCD, IGST, cess and trade remedy duties but is subject to actual user condition.

questions.prompt: What is the value addition achieved by Sunrise under its Advance Authorisation, and does it meet the general minimum?
options: 30%; yes
30%; no, as the minimum is 40%
questions.explanation: VA = (A - B) / B x 100 = (2,60,00,000 - 2,00,00,000) / 2,00,00,000 x 100 = 30%. The general minimum under AA is 15%, so it is met. 23.08% would be the result of wrongly dividing by A.

questions.prompt: Within what period must Sunrise fulfil the specific export obligation under its EPCG authorisation?
options: 18 months
3 years
6 years
8 years
questions.explanation: Under the EPCG scheme, the specific export obligation of 6 times the duties, taxes and cess saved must be fulfilled within 6 years from the date of issue of the authorisation.

questions.prompt: RoDTEP benefit is credited as a transferable electronic duty credit scrip that can be used to pay basic customs duty on imports.
questions.explanation: RoDTEP rebates are issued as e-scrips in the exporter's electronic ledger on ICEGATE. They are freely transferable and can be used to pay BCD on imported goods.

questions.prompt: Which of these taxes are meant to be refunded through RoDTEP?
options: VAT on fuel used to transport export goods
Electricity duty on power used in manufacture
Mandi tax on agricultural inputs
IGST paid on export of goods
Basic customs duty paid on imported inputs refunded by drawback
questions.explanation: RoDTEP covers embedded duties and taxes not refunded under any other mechanism, such as VAT on fuel, electricity duty and mandi tax. IGST on exports is refunded under GST law, and BCD on inputs is covered by duty drawback.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: under the EPCG scheme, the specific export obligation equals ___ times the duties, taxes and cess saved on the capital goods.
questions.explanation: The specific export obligation is 6 times the duties, taxes and cess saved, fulfilled within 6 years. It is reduced by 25% when capital goods are sourced from Indian manufacturers.

questions.prompt: Compute the specific export obligation in ₹ lakh (round to 2 decimals).
questions.data: An exporter procures capital goods from an Indian manufacturer under the EPCG scheme. Duties, taxes and cess saved: ₹40 lakh.
questions.explanation:
| Particulars | ₹ lakh |
| --- | --- |
| Normal EO: 6 x 40 | 240 |
| Less: 25% for domestic sourcing | (60) |
| **Specific EO** | **180** |

To be fulfilled within 6 years, in addition to the average export obligation.

questions.prompt: Compute the RoDTEP benefit on the shipment (round to the nearest rupee).
questions.data: FOB value of an export shipment: USD 50,000. Exchange rate notified by CBIC for exports: ₹85 per USD. Assume the notified RoDTEP rate for the product is 1.2% of FOB with no value cap.
questions.explanation:
| Particulars | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- |
| FOB in ₹: 50,000 x 85 | 42,50,000 |
| RoDTEP at 1.2% | 51,000 |

The amount is credited as an e-scrip usable for BCD.

questions.prompt: Compute Sunrise's specific export obligation under EPCG, in ₹ lakh (round to 2 decimals). The capital goods were imported, not sourced domestically.
questions.explanation: Specific EO = 6 x duties, taxes and cess saved = 6 x ₹80 lakh = ₹480 lakh (₹4.8 crore), within 6 years. IGST saved is included in the base.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a deemed export under the Foreign Trade Policy?
options: Supply of goods to a customer in Nepal against rupee payment
Supply of goods by a domestic manufacturer to an Advance Authorisation holder against that authorisation
Sale of goods to a foreign tourist at an airport shop
Sale of goods on the high seas before customs clearance
questions.explanation: Deemed exports are supplies where goods do not leave India, such as supplies to AA holders, EOUs and EPCG holders against their authorisations. Supplies to Nepal are physical exports; high seas sales are outside GST under Schedule III.

questions.prompt: Compute the duty saved, test the value addition and state the key conditions for Kanak Exports' Advance Authorisation.
questions.data: Kanak Exports holds an Advance Authorisation. It imports inputs of CIF value ₹1,00,00,000 duty-free and later exports finished goods, realising FOB ₹1,25,00,000. Without the authorisation, the inputs would attract BCD 10%, SWS 10% of BCD and IGST 18%.
questions.answer:
**Duty saved**

| Particulars | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- |
| Assessable value | 1,00,00,000 |
| BCD 10% | 10,00,000 |
| SWS 10% of BCD | 1,00,000 |
| IGST 18% of 1,11,00,000 | 19,98,000 |
| **Total duty saved** | **30,98,000** |

**Value addition:** VA = (1,25,00,000 - 1,00,00,000) / 1,00,00,000 x 100 = **25%**, above the 15% minimum, so the export obligation in value terms is met.

**Conditions:** inputs must be physically incorporated in the export product as per SION or ad hoc norms; imports within 12 months of issue; export obligation within 18 months; actual user condition (inputs not transferable); on fulfilment, the holder applies for redemption (EODC). If the obligation is not met, duty saved is paid with interest.

questions.prompt: Explain the EPCG scheme under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023.
questions.answer:
- **Objective:** to let exporters import capital goods for pre-production, production and post-production at zero customs duty, to improve competitiveness.
- **Coverage:** capital goods including spares, tools, refractories and software; also domestic sourcing of capital goods.
- **Duties exempted:** BCD, IGST, compensation cess and other duties on the capital goods.
- **Specific export obligation:** 6 times the duties, taxes and cess saved, within 6 years from issue; 25% less for domestic sourcing.
- **Average export obligation:** over and above the average exports of the preceding 3 years for the same and similar products.
- **Conditions:** actual user condition until the obligation is met; exports must use the capital goods; block-wise fulfilment of the obligation.
- **Default:** duty saved is payable with interest, and the authorisation holder faces penal action under the FT(D&R) Act.

questions.prompt: What are the key features of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023?
questions.answer:
- **Open-ended policy** from 1 April 2023, updated as needed instead of every five years.
- **Incentive to remission:** schemes like RoDTEP and RoSCTL refund embedded taxes, in line with WTO rules, instead of reward schemes.
- **Collaboration:** Districts as Export Hubs with district export action plans; new Towns of Export Excellence; role for States and Indian missions.
- **Ease of doing business:** automatic online approvals, lower application fees for MSMEs, and reduced thresholds for status holders (One Star at USD 3 million up to Five Star at USD 800 million).
- **Emerging areas:** e-commerce exports with a higher courier value limit, merchanting trade, and streamlined SCOMET controls for dual-use goods.
- **Amnesty scheme** for default in export obligations under AA and EPCG.
- Continuation of Advance Authorisation, DFIA, EPCG and EOU schemes with simplifications.
